slides.headline: Simon Judd built for this moment.
slides.line: Index Coop scale, GPU cryptography, and EPFL systems research led to Katechon.
slides.narration: Katechon founder Simon Judd helped grow Index Coop to five hundred million dollars in AUM and raise ten million dollars. He then spent three years deep in GPU acceleration, cryptography, and computer science at Ingonyama and EPFL. That mix of distribution and systems depth is why Katechon exists.

slides.headline: Code hit the camera moment.
slides.line: AI makes software cheap enough to generate continuously around user interests.
slides.narration: The iPhone made photos functionally infinite, and Instagram made them living objects. AI is doing the same to code: software can now be generated continuously, in real time, around what each user wants to understand or do.

slides.headline: Screenshots are the wrong container.
slides.line: The dashboards people share should stay live, personalized, and actionable.
slides.narration: Today that software has no native container. People vibe-code dashboards for major events, then post screenshots and videos. Katechon keeps the dashboard alive so the next viewer can inspect it, personalize it, and act inside it.

slides.headline: Live software channels.
slides.line: Each channel materializes as code when the user navigates to it.
slides.narration: In this demo, every dashboard and board is treated as software materializing in real time as the user navigates: intelligence rooms, markets, agents, science, and culture, all shaped by user interest and narrated by Kat.

slides.headline: Own discovery for generated software.
slides.line: Crypto trading, prediction markets, and token launchpads become native channel actions.
slides.imageAlt: A cinematic software feed control plane connecting frontier model cores to live software channels and audience signals.
slides.narration: Every new media format made its biggest company at discovery. As users watch and use Katechon, we learn which models, prompts, tools, states, and intents become software channels. And because wallets and transactions can live inside those channels, Katechon is a natural distribution layer for crypto trading, prediction markets, and token launchpads.

The whole scene feels like owning the algorithmic layer between models and users.
